messages.author: 2f40ed71ed2c3b06
messages.subject: indirect effect with multiple groups
parts:
First of all, thank you for the wonderful package!

  Anyhow, I found that when I do multiple group analysis with FIML missing with indirect effect,

  indirect effects are only reported once rather than for each groups...

  It seems like there's a little bug...

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: indirect effect with multiple groups
parts:
That doesn't seem likely.  Note that you would need to label each group's relevant direct effects in your model syntax, then define the indirect separately for each group in your model syntax.  If that is what you are doing and you don't see all of the indirect effects you defined in your syntax when you print results, please post your R script (and perhaps some data) that reproduces this.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Can I label each group's relevant direct effects? 

  In the manual, https://dornsife.usc.edu/assets/sites/210/docs/GC3/lavaan_tutorial.pdf

  I couldn't find how to do it...

  Here's my code and data

df <- read.csv( file="sample.csv")

theModel <- "
bidToEst ~ b2*n.bidder + est + b4*DM
CO ~ b1*bidToEst + est + DM
indirect1 := b1*b4
"

theFitMissing <- sem(theModel, data=df, group="PT1", meanstructure = T, 
                     missing="fiml", estimator="MLR")

summary(theFitMissing)
